foodDescription: Thick fries cooked twice, sold in paper cones from a frietkot, a fry stand, with mayonnaise or another sauce. Two stands have sold them below the belfry for decades.
Beef stewed slowly in dark beer with onions and a slice of bread spread with mustard. Served with fries.
A pot of mussels steamed with celery and onion, with fries on the side. Best from September to April.
Croquettes filled with tiny gray North Sea shrimp in a creamy sauce, served with fried parsley and lemon.
Eel cooked in a sauce of sorrel, parsley, chervil, and other green herbs. An old Flemish dish.
A creamy stew of chicken or fish with vegetables, originally from Ghent and found across Flanders.
Brussels waffles are light and rectangular, eaten with toppings. Liège waffles are dense and sweet with pearl sugar, eaten plain.
Filled chocolates, invented in Belgium in 1912. Bruges has dozens of chocolate shops, some making everything by hand.
Thin, crisp, lacy cookies of butter, brown sugar, and almonds. A Bruges specialty.
Thin, crunchy biscuits spiced with cinnamon. Often served with coffee.
A blond beer brewed in the center of Bruges by De Halve Maan. Its name is the old nickname for the people of Bruges.
The Low Countries’ juniper spirit, the ancestor of gin. Drunk cold, in small tulip glasses, often in fruit flavors.
